findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search, get_insider_trades, get_institution, get_politician, list_filings, list_short_interest · Private data: get_insider_trades, get_institution, get_politician_trades, get_politician, list_filings · Public sink: get_stock, get_stock_13f_holders, get_institution, get_superinvestor_activity, get_major_holders, get_form144_notices, get_financials, get_short_interest, screen_stocks · Destructive: get_ownership_filings.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search, get_insider_trades, get_institution, get_politician, list_filings, list_short_interest · Private data: get_insider_trades, get_institution, get_politician_trades, get_politician, list_filings · Public sink: get_stock, get_stock_13f_holders, get_institution, get_superinvestor_activity, get_major_holders, get_form144_notices, get_financials, get_short_interest, screen_stocks · Destructive: get_ownership_filings

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
